html:
England became a single kingdom in 927, when the West Saxon king Æthelstan brought the last Viking ruled lands under his rule. It merged with Scotland into Great Britain in 1707 and became, in the 1800s, the centre of the largest empire in history.

The Anglo-Saxon kingdom was conquered twice: by the Danish king Cnut in 1016, and in the Norman conquest of 1066, which gave England a French speaking ruling class. Barons forced King John to accept Magna Carta in 1215, an early limit on royal power, and Parliament grew out of royal councils in the following century.

Turning points:

  • Henry VIII broke with Rome in the 1530s; his daughter Elizabeth I settled a Protestant church.
  • Civil war in the 1640s, a king executed in 1649, and the 1688 revolution that left Parliament supreme.
  • Union with Scotland in 1707, and with Ireland in 1801, making the United Kingdom.
  • The Bank of England (1694) and a strong system of public debt paid for long wars with France.

Britain was the first country to industrialise. The agricultural revolution, coal, cotton and steam power made it the workshop of the world, and London the centre of world trade and finance. The empire grew fast under Victoria, and by the 1920s it covered about a quarter of the world's land.

Most of Ireland left in 1922. Britain fought both world wars, standing alone against Nazi Germany in 1940 under Winston Churchill, and gave up most of its empire after 1945.
